dates_external_review_wire: Core's genuine bodies of the D-149 review contract - members'
corrections (the app's side, member-*) and the console's side (webadmin-*):
- the external list and detail with the external admin contract selector v2;
- the "reviewed, OK" mark;
- the corrections queue, a rejection, and the three approvals (an edit, a cancellation, an official
  update) with `correction_id`;
- the AI re-research of one event, its receipt, its refusals, and a detail in each job state;
- the system's closure of research intakes (`system_closure`) and, since the yield round, the
  run candidates' `drop_detail`;
- the yield round's details of a festival span, an ongoing exhibition and a date-only (all-day)
  event, with the member side of contract 3;
- with their refusals.

Source: Core tests/fixtures/dates_external_review_wire at commit
        ef10bc77 ("Rebind every wire corpus to live b5784fca plus the yield lane; capture contract 3")
        on the yield lane branch claude/areyouin-research-yield-20261102 (local, not yet published when
        copied on 2026-11-02).

        The corpus was generated at d9f54d59 (manifest.json, `source_commit`) by
        tests/dates_external_review_fixture_dump.php. That is real HTTP through public/index.php under
        PHP's own web server, two captures compared byte for byte. It used the console's form transport
        with its secret and both selectors (manifest.json `selectors.webadmin`).

How:    BYTE COPIES of the 90 bodies and manifest.json of that directory, extracted with
        `git archive ef10bc77 tests/fixtures`; nothing was edited.

        tests/datesExternalReviewWire.test.mts checks every body against the sha256 the manifest
        names and the manifest's `fixture_set_sha256`. It also checks that this directory holds
        nothing else but this note.

        The member-* bodies are the app's side; they are kept so that the copy is whole.

Changed against the previous pin (Core-B 1735a158, 77 bodies):
- webadmin-research-run-detail-system-closure.json gains `"drop_detail": null` after each
  `system_closure`;
- 13 new bodies: 10 member (date-only on contract 3, festival, ongoing exhibition, joining it) and 3
  console details (festival, exhibition-ongoing, date-only).
Every other body is byte-identical.
